title: Aseptic Meningitis, Mucocutaneous Lesions and Arthritis after COVID-19 Vaccination in a 15-Year-Old Boy
case_prompt:
A 15-year-old boy presented 13 days after his second dose of the BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccine with a 3-day history of acute headache and 1 day of fever, nausea, vomiting, and painful oral aphthous ulcers. Ibuprofen provided no relief. His medical history was unremarkable except for knee cartilage surgery one month earlier and several tick bites; vaccinations were up to date, including varicella. 

On admission, temperature was 38.8 °C. He had neck rigidity with positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs. Oral aphthous ulcers were seen on his lips, tongue, and inner cheeks. The remainder of the neurologic and skin examination was unremarkable. 

Laboratory studies showed: 
- White blood cells 10,920/μL (neutrophils 8,980/μL)  
- C-reactive protein 5.34 mg/dL (reference < 0.3 mg/dL)  
- Procalcitonin < 0.5 μg/L  

Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed: 
- 242 cells/μL (109 granulocytes, 133 lymphomononuclear)  
- Protein 69.4 mg/dL (reference 15–40 mg/dL)  
- Lactate 2.92 mmol/L (normal)  
- Glucose 65 mg/dL (normal)  
- Elevated CSF/serum IgA and IgM indices  

Broad microbiological and virological testing, including bacterial cultures, 16S rDNA PCR, PCR for HSV-1/2, HHV-6/7, parvovirus B19, EBV, VZV, CMV, enterovirus, parechovirus, adenovirus, norovirus, measles, mumps, tick-borne encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, and next-generation sequencing for pathogens, was negative. Serologies for VZV, HSV, CMV, EBV, and Borrelia burgdorferi (including CSF CXCL13) were negative. PCR and serology for acute or prior SARS-CoV-2 infection were unremarkable.

Over the next three days, he developed a faint maculopapular rash on his cheeks, erythema nodosum–like lesions and a pustule on his lower legs, and right knee swelling; ultrasound showed echo-free effusion. He reported floaters, but ophthalmologic exam showed no uveitis, and optical coherence tomography revealed only minimal posterior vitreous inhomogeneities. Brain MRI demonstrated slight pachy- and leptomeningeal enhancement without other abnormalities. Autoimmune studies (rheumatoid factor, ANA, pANCA, cANCA, anti–dsDNA) and HLA-B51 genotyping were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Bacterial meningitis — “Broad microbiological ... screening included negative bacterial cultures and 16S ribosomal DNA-PCR … did not identify any causative pathogen.”  
2. Viral meningitis — “Virological PCR analyses for HSV-1/2, HHV-6/7, parvovirus B19, EBV, VZV, CMV, entero-, parecho-, adeno-, noro-, measles, mumps, FSME-, and west-nil-virus … did not identify any causative pathogen.”  
3. Neuroborreliosis — “Serological analyses did not reveal evidence for acute infections ... B. burgdorferi (the latter including negative chemokine CXCL13 in CSF and persistently negative IgM and IgG).”  
4. COVID-19–associated meningitis — “PCR and serological tests for an acute and/or prior COVID-19 infection were also unremarkable.”  
5. Behçet’s disease — “Based on the current clinical scoring system ... our patient has an ICBD-score of 4 ... which is exactly the cutoff value (≥4) to indicate a Behçet’s Disease diagnosis ... older diagnostic criteria ... would not have allowed the diagnosis ... because of the lack of recurrent symptoms.”
